reader.requirement: At --std 85 a successful REWRITE releases the replacing logical record to the operating system: the physical file holds it at once in place of the replaced record, with the record count unchanged, so a later READ through this or another file connector of the same physical file sees it.

edition-consulted.switches: SharingFacilityInEffect: from 2002 another run unit may write, so the reader always re-anchors; at 85 it re-anchors only when the physical file's release generation moved (NoteRelease)
the OPEN's default sharing mode; AllOther at 85 lets the second connector open the file beside the I-O one

reader.edition-search: grep of Edition|SharingFacilityInEffect in SequentialConnector.cs; OverwriteInPlace (seek, write, Flush, NoteRelease) is edition-free.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf27_01 checks the record after CLOSE and reopen; a second connector reading while the I-O connector is still open, and the variable-length record, are not exercised by it

probes.printed: RW 00; F2 (second file-name on the same physical file, opened INPUT while F is open I-O) SEES NEWB 00
probes.expected: the record released at the REWRITE is in the physical file

probes.printed: variable-length records read back 03XXX / 06BBBBBB / 02ZZ: the rewritten records replaced in place, the count unchanged
probes.expected: the released records replace the read ones

citations.check: OK  §1985:VII.4.5.4 GR8  (4.5.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR8

reader.notes: The one in-place overwrite flushes the stream before answering 00 and announces the release so sibling connectors re-anchor; at 85 the re-anchor is driven by the release generation, which the probe showed suffices for a second connector in the same run unit.

refuter.evidence: Read SequentialConnector.OverwriteInPlace (Flush then NoteRelease) and the SharingFacilityInEffect arm (line 376). q5stale.cob at --std 85 with BLOCK CONTAINS 4 RECORDS: F2 opened INPUT and READ record 1 BEFORE F (open I-O) rewrote records 3, 4 and 5; F2's later READs show OLD02, NEW03, NEW04, NEW05 (no stale read-ahead). q4sra.cob: a separately compiled program opens the physical file INPUT while FA is still open I-O and sees NEW2. q3rw.cob: variable-length (4 TO 8) blocked records rewritten in place, count unchanged. cite.py: OK §1985:VII.4.5.4 GR8 'releases a logical record to the operating system'.
